recommendation: Keep the empty no-change audit commit. If additional tutorial examples are desired, handle them in the cross-version extension guide or FAQ rather than duplicating guide-owned guidance in core versions.html.
issue_request: Published/Persuasive FHIR-core compatibility issue requesting clarification that a future BackboneElement backported as a cross-version extension should be represented as a complex extension whose child extensions are named after the backbone element's component properties, using ValueSet.expansion.contains.property as the example.
initial_application: Commit 526d8c02b309fb11b45bbfc4b60f7da0b491b935 applied the issue by adding complex-extension child-property guidance to source/versions.html. The same commit also touched a patient example, but the relevant application was the versions.html compatibility wording.
additional_context: Later same-section issues FHIR-31721 and FHIR-36702 expanded inter-version extension guidance. Commit f45505e5b3aa0d87effb991938750e627b782d2d intentionally removed the detailed inline examples and rules from source/versions.html because the cross-version content moved to the individual cross-version definition guides. The current active core page still defines the URL pattern and points to those packages, and hl7.fhir.uv.xver-r5.r4 0.1.0 formally defines the ValueSet.expansion.contains.property extension with code, value, and subProperty child slices.
reconciliation: No source change was made. The current core source is correct in its present architecture: versions.html delegates the details to the xver packages, and the issue's example BackboneElement is represented there using the requested child-name pattern.
